steps.title: Import React, createContext, useContext, useState, and useCallback
steps.instruction: Add import statements for React, createContext, useContext, useState, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the names in curly braces and the module path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports to use React, context creation, context consumption, state management, and callback memoization.
successCriteria: React, createContext, useContext, useState, and useCallback are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported all the React APIs needed for creating and using context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some of the required APIs. Make sure to import React, createContext, useContext, useState, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or missing. You need to import React, createContext, useContext, useState, and useCallback from 'react'.

steps.title: Create NotificationContext using createContext
steps.instruction: Create a context named NotificationContext using React.createContext() with default values of null for both state and setState.
steps.hint: Call createContext from React and assign it to a const variable. Provide an object with state and setState properties as the default value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a context with default values
const UserContext = React.createContext({ user: null, setUser: () => {} });
steps.seedCode:
import React, { createContext, useContext, useState, useCallback } from 'react';

// Create NotificationContext here
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationContext variable is created with createContext, ready to hold notification state and functions.
successCriteria: NotificationContext is defined using React.createContext with an object containing state: null and setState: null as default values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the NotificationContext with proper default values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You created a context, but check the default values. It should be an object with state and setState properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The context wasn't created correctly. Use React.createContext() with an object containing state: null and setState: null.

steps.title: Create NotificationProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named NotificationProvider that takes children as props and returns them wrapped in a div.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a children prop and returns JSX containing that children prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationProvider component is defined that accepts children and returns them wrapped in a div.
successCriteria: The NotificationProvider function component is created with the correct name, accepts children as props, and returns children wrapped in a div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the NotificationProvider component that will wrap your app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component is named exactly 'NotificationProvider', accepts children as props, and returns them wrapped in a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function named NotificationProvider that takes children and returns JSX containing them.

steps.title: Initialize notification state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationProvider component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'notification' with an initial value of null.
steps.hint: Call useState(null) and destructure the returned array into a variable named 'notification' and a setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for a message
const [message, setMessage] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider component will have a state variable 'notification' initialized to null, ready to store notification data.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with null as initial value, and the returned array is destructured into 'notification' and a setter function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the notification state. This will allow the provider to track the current notification message and visibility.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with null as the initial value and destructuring the array into 'notification' and a setter function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside NotificationProvider, use useState(null) to create a state variable named 'notification'.

steps.title: Create showNotification function
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationProvider component, create a function named showNotification that takes a 'message' parameter and updates the notification state with that message.
steps.hint: Define the function using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should set the notification state to the provided message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider component now contains a showNotification function that will be used to display notifications by updating the state.
successCriteria: A function named showNotification is defined inside NotificationProvider that takes a message parameter and sets the notification state with that message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the showNotification function. This function will allow components to trigger notifications by calling it with a message.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your showNotification function takes a message parameter and updates the notification state with that message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The showNotification function isn't quite right. It should be defined inside NotificationProvider, take a message parameter, and update the notification state with that message.

steps.title: Create hideNotification function
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationProvider component, create a function named hideNotification that sets the notification state back to null.
steps.hint: You can define a function that calls the state setter function with null as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider component now contains a hideNotification function that will clear the notification state.
successCriteria: A hideNotification function is defined inside NotificationProvider that sets notification state to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the hideNotification function that will clear notifications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a function, but make sure it's named exactly 'hideNotification' and sets the notification state to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hideNotification function is missing or doesn't set the notification state to null. Try creating a function that calls the state setter with null.

steps.title: Memoize functions with useCallback
steps.instruction: Wrap your existing showNotification and hideNotification functions with useCallback to memoize them.
steps.hint: Use useCallback to wrap each function, passing the function as the first argument and an empty dependency array as the second.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both showNotification and hideNotification functions are wrapped with useCallback to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
successCriteria: showNotification and hideNotification are memoized using useCallback with empty dependency arrays.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully memoized both functions with useCallback, which will optimize performance by preventing unnecessary re-creations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've memoized one function, but remember to wrap both showNotification and hideNotification with useCallback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The functions need to be wrapped with useCallback. Check that you're using the useCallback hook with an empty dependency array for both functions.

steps.title: Create context value object
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationProvider component, create a value object containing the notification state, showNotification function, and hideNotification function, then pass it to the Provider's value prop.
steps.hint: The value object should include all three pieces: the notification state variable, and the two memoized functions. Make sure to reference the actual variable and function names you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationProvider will have a complete value object ready to be provided to consuming components through the context.
successCriteria: A value object is created containing notification, showNotification, and hideNotification, and this object is passed to the Provider's value prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the context value object with all the necessary data and functions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your value object includes all three items: notification, showNotification, and hideNotification.
steps.feedbackWrong: The value object isn't complete or correctly structured. Check that you're including the notification state and both memoized functions.

steps.title: Return NotificationContext.Provider with value
steps.instruction: In the NotificationProvider component, pass the context value object you created to the NotificationContext.Provider's value prop.
steps.hint: The value prop should receive the object containing notification, showNotification, and hideNotification.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationContext.Provider will have a value prop containing the notification state and functions.
successCriteria: The NotificationContext.Provider's value prop is set to an object with notification, showNotification, and hideNotification properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed the context value to the provider, making it available to all child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the value prop contains an object with all three properties: notification, showNotification, and hideNotification.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationContext.Provider still has an empty value object. Pass the complete context value containing notification state and functions.

steps.title: Create useNotification custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook named 'useNotification' that returns the result of calling useContext with NotificationContext.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses useContext to access the notification context value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook is created that provides access to the notification context.
successCriteria: The useNotification function is defined and returns useContext(NotificationContext).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a custom hook that will make it easy to access the notification context from any component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your hook returns the result of useContext(NotificationContext).
steps.feedbackWrong: The useNotification hook should be a function that returns useContext(NotificationContext).

steps.title: Create NotificationDisplay component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named NotificationDisplay that uses the useNotification hook to access the notification state and returns a paragraph element displaying the notification message.
steps.hint: Define a component that calls useNotification to get the notification value, then conditionally render a paragraph with the message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationDisplay component is created that uses the useNotification hook and returns a paragraph element.
successCriteria: NotificationDisplay component is defined, uses useNotification hook, and returns a paragraph element with the notification message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the NotificationDisplay component that will show notifications from context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the component but may be missing the useNotification hook call or the paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationDisplay component is not properly defined. Make sure to create a functional component that uses useNotification and returns a paragraph.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering and close button to NotificationDisplay
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationDisplay component, add conditional rendering to only show the notification when there's a message, and include a close button that calls hideNotification when clicked.
steps.hint: Use a conditional (like &&) to render the notification UI only if notification exists. Add a button with an onClick handler that calls hideNotification.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationDisplay component will show a notification message with a close button only when notification exists, and clicking the button will hide it.
successCriteria: NotificationDisplay uses conditional rendering to show UI only when notification exists, includes a button with onClick={hideNotification}, and returns JSX with the notification message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've completed the NotificationDisplay component with conditional rendering and a working close button.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to add both the conditional rendering (check if notification exists) and a button that calls hideNotification when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationDisplay component is missing either conditional rendering or the close button functionality. Review the instructions.
